en: The Blood Bowl Sūtra of the Orthodox Teachings from the Great Canon Spoken by the Buddha.

At that time, the Venerable Maudgalyāyana traveled to Chu-yang County in Yu-zhou in a former life and beheld a Blood Bowl Hell eighty-four thousand yojanas wide, within which were one hundred and twenty iron beams.

Seeing many women of Jambudvīpa with disheveled hair and long shackles upon their hands suffering punishment in hell—iron pillars, iron collars, and iron chains—the Hell-Warden King leads them three times each day to force-feed them blood.
At this, the sinners are unwilling to submit and eat; consequently, they are struck with iron clubs by the Lord of Hell.
Making a cry of distress, Maudgalyāyana asked the warden of the hells in sorrow: "I do not see men from Jambudvīpa undergoing such retribution for their suffering;
I see only these many women experiencing such agony. The warden replied to the Master: "This does not concern the affairs of men;
it is only because women give birth to blood and impurities that they defile the earth deities. If they are thus polluted—"

One takes their garments to wash in a stream or river; the flowing water becomes turbid and defiled, causing those good men and women who take the water to brew tea as an offering to the various sages to receive something impure.

Consequently, the Great General of Heaven records their names on a tally and attaches them to the registers of the virtuous and the wicked, so that after a hundred years at the end of their lives, they must undergo this retribution of suffering. Maudgalyāyana was filled with sorrow and thus questioned him.
The Lord of Hell asked, "How shall you repay the kindness of your mother who gave birth to you?

The one who had escaped from the Blood Basin Hell replied to the Master, saying, "I shall only be careful and filial; I will ensure that my sons and daughters revere the Triple Gem, and for three years I shall observe the Blood Basin Fast for my mother.
Furthermore, I will convene a superior Blood Basin Assembly and invite monks to recite this sutra one entire collection."
When the days of the ritual are complete and the repentance is concluded, one immediately boards the boat of Prajñā to cross the river and reach the bank.
There, one beholds five lotus flowers emerging from the Blood Basin Pond; the sinner feels joy and gives rise to a sense of shame and remorse, thereby attaining rebirth in the Buddha-ground.
Then the great Bodhisattvas and the Venerable Maudgalyāyana come to exhort the people of Jambudvīpa.

Faithful sons and daughters of good family, awaken early and cultivate yourselves to secure a great future; do not let your hands falter, for it would be difficult to recover from such a loss for ten thousand kalpas.

The Buddha told them: "If there are those with faith who copy and uphold this *Blood Basin Sūtra* for women, they shall cause all mothers of the three periods of time to be reborn in heaven and enjoy all manner of happiness.
Their food, clothing, and wealth will be provided spontaneously, and they shall attain long life and nobility. At that time...
The devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, and others were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced [the teaching], paid homage, and withdrew.
This concludes the *Blood Bowl Sūtra* (Xiěpén jīng), the True Teaching of the Great Canon, as spoken by the Buddha.
